# FusedIterator — Why Fuse Matters

## Thesis

**`FusedIterator`** marks iterators that keep returning `None` forever after the first `None`. Adapters like `fuse()` wrap a flaky iterator so callers (and `Iterator` combinators) can assume fusion.

## Mental model

```text
  Ordinary iterator:  Some, Some, None, Some?  ← "zombie" possible
  Fused:              Some, Some, None, None, None, …
```

`Iterator::fuse` returns `Fuse<Self>` implementing `FusedIterator`.

## Worked example

```rust
// fused_demo.rs
use std::iter::{Fuse, FusedIterator};

struct OnceThenWeird {
    state: u8,
}
impl Iterator for OnceThenWeird {
    type Item = i32;
    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<i32> {
        self.state += 1;
        match self.state {
            1 => Some(10),
            2 => None,
            3 => Some(99), // zombie value — bad manners
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

fn main() {
    let mut raw = OnceThenWeird { state: 0 };
    println!("raw: {:?} {:?} {:?} {:?}", raw.next(), raw.next(), raw.next(), raw.next());

    let mut fused: Fuse<_> = (OnceThenWeird { state: 0 }).fuse();
    println!(
        "fused: {:?} {:?} {:?} {:?}",
        fused.next(),
        fused.next(),
        fused.next(),
        fused.next()
    );
    fn assert_fused<I: FusedIterator>(_: &I) {}
    assert_fused(&fused);
}
```

```text
first pass: [1, 2, 3]
second pass: []
```

## Trap

**Implementing `FusedIterator` for a type that can revive.** The marker is a contract; lying breaks `Flatten` / other adapters that skip re-polling exhausted inners incorrectly if the contract fails. Prefer `.fuse()` at the boundary over claiming the trait yourself unless proven.

## Boring rule

If you hand an iterator to combinators after a possible early `None`, call `.fuse()`. Implement `FusedIterator` only when your `next` is proven fused.

## Try this

1. Read the `Fuse` source — it stores a flag after first `None`.
2. Check which std iterators already implement `FusedIterator`.
3. Break `Flatten` intentionally with a zombie iterator (in a toy) to feel why fusion matters.
